name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
note: Seven Cypriot kings paid tribute to Assyria from 709–707 BCE

name: Saite Egypt
note: Amasis made Cyprus tributary around 560 BCE

name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
note: Cyprus lay within the Persian province 'Beyond the River'

name: Empire of Alexander
note: The Cypriot kings joined Alexander after Issus

name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
note: Cyprus was governed by a Ptolemaic strategos; the Antigonids held it 306–294 BCE

name: Roman Empire
note: A senatorial province under a proconsul from 22 BCE

name: Eastern Roman Empire
note: Ruled from Constantinople; Salamis-Constantia was the capital

name: Umayyad Caliphate
note: Raided from 649; from 688 shared the island's taxes with Byzantium

name: Byzantine Empire
note: Byzantium kept a claim and a share of the taxes through the shared period

name: Abbasid Caliphate
note: Shared the island's taxes with Byzantium until 965

name: Byzantine Empire
note: Cyprus was a Byzantine theme from 965

name: Mamluk Sultanate
note: Cyprus paid tribute to Cairo after 1426

name: Venetian Republic
note: Cyprus was Venice's largest overseas possession

name: Ottoman Empire
note: An Ottoman province, later a sanjak

name: British Empire
note: British administration from 1878, annexed 1914, Crown Colony 1925
